messages:
olivia: paging: autoscaler alerts firing in us-west-2, multiple GPU pools showing ThrottleErrors and failed scale-ups. Impact: request queuing and elevated tail latency. Investigating now. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: [AUTOMATED] PagerDuty incident created: PD-8442. Notifying oncall schedule.
ramon: I'm oncall, acked PD-8442. First look — logs show several 403s from cloud quota API and a bunch of VM preemptions.
mira: seeing degraded ingress to dedicated pools, requests backed up ~60s. Customers in EU are fine. Seems regional to us-west-2.
sre-oncall: quick handoff: I'm joining the bridge in 1m. If autoscaler can't provision new instances we'll need short-term eviction to spare capacity.
evan: adding context — we shipped a deployment to the serving runtime yesterday that increases GPU memory footprint for some small models. Could be coincident but noting it.
olivia: @ramon can you confirm whether this is autoscaler failing or infra preemption storms? Logs?
ramon: checking cluster events: lots of 'instance terminated by host' and then quota denied when trying to create replacement VMs: 
```
kube-events: NodePreempted: instance-az3-xxx terminated by host
cloud-api: quotaExceeded: GPUs per project limit reached
```
mira: so two things: (1) cloud preemptions causing churn -> autoscaler hits quota limits when creating replacements; (2) serving runtime memory bump is increasing per-node GPU usage which reduces thin provisioning headroom.
sre-oncall: mitigation plan in-flight: 1) temporarily route lower-priority traffic to warm fallback models in other regions, 2) throttle large-batch jobs on dedicated pools, 3) request emergency quota bump with cloud provider. Initiating 1 & 2 now.
olivia: executed traffic routing change: `route-policy set --region us-west-2 fallback=true priority>=low` — responses improving for critical paths. :thumbsup:
ev an: I've opened cloud support case CS-99824 asking for immediate GPU quota increase and linked incidents. ETA unknown, but support acknowledged.
incident-bot: [UPDATE] Bridge started by ramon at 1779998910. Recording notes to incident channel.
mira: created a temporary autoscaler override to reduce per-node binpacking for the affected pools (`autoscaler/profile=evac-temp, max-surge=0.2`). Will monitor.
sre-oncall: early customer impact: a handful of mid-tier customers saw 25-40% higher tail latency for 20 minutes starting 1779998840. No data loss. Product Ops, please reach out with a short note.
product-ops: drafting a customer message now — will route to success for affected accounts. Suggest offering a credit for margin hits.
ramon: traffic and latency trending down after the routing change and autoscaler override. Need to validate stability for 30m before full rollback.
olivia: agreed. next steps for post-incident: schedule postmortem, track root cause and a remediation plan (short-term and long-term), and create follow-up jira tasks.
mira: short-term action items I will take: (A) revert serving runtime memory bump for the small-model config in us-west-2 canary (owner: mira), (B) maintain autoscaler override until quota confirmed/eviction risk drops (owner: mira).
ev an: infra action items: (C) coordinate with cloud to get quota bump and request backup capacity in adjacent AZ, case CS-99824 (owner: evan), (D) add preemption-aware probe to autoscaler to reduce simultaneous replacement attempts (owner: ramon).
olivia: product ops / success: (E) customer outreach note + credit proposal (owner: product-ops).
ramon: I'll own the postmortem writeup & timeline (owner: ramon). Proposing postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT — can folks confirm availability?
judy: I can make tomorrow 10:00 PT. I'll bring deployment and rollout logs for the serving runtime bump.
mira: confirmed for 10:00 PT.
ev an: confirmed.
sre-oncall: tentative 10:00 PT is fine for me.
olivia: OK scheduled: Postmortem meeting created — link: https://company.jira.com/meetings/PM-8442 (calendar invite sent).
ramon: creating follow-up jira tasks now: 
- RW-12540: Revert canary memory bump for small-model config in us-west-2 (owner: mira, sev: high, due: +1d)
- RW-12541: Autoscaler preemption probe and backoff logic (owner: ramon, sev: medium, due: +7d)
- RW-12542: Cloud quota emergency process doc + runbook update (owner: evan, sev: medium, due: +3d)
- RW-12543: Customer outreach and credit orchestration (owner: product-ops, sev: low, due: +2d)
mira: adding runbook note: update capacity playbook with 'reduce simultaneous replacement attempts' and 'autoscaler fallback to other regions' steps.
olivia: tagging for follow-up: please add post-incident quality checks to Redwood Optimize suggestions — model changes that increase memory by >5% should trigger a capacity impact review. (owner: product)
ev an: noted. Will add an automated pre-merge check to the model config pipeline.
ramon: retrospective checklist items to include in postmortem: timeline, decision log (why revert vs roll forward), customer impact quant (requests affected, accounts), and concrete remediation owners+due dates.
olivia: verdict: incident resolved at 1779999020, queue depths normal, autoscaler stable. We keep the jira tasks and schedule the postmortem.
incident-bot: [RESOLVED] PD-8442 resolved by ramon at 1779999020. Please complete post-incident review within 72 hours.
mira: quick note — we'll keep autoscaler override until cloud confirms quota bump or until 177999+86400 (24h), whichever comes first.
ramon: wrapping up: I'll post a short summary in #incidents after the writeup and link all RW JIRA items. Thanks for fast responses — nice work. :clap:
olivia: thanks everyone. Leaving final ownership list here for the postmortem doc: owners: ramon (postmortem + autoscaler probe), mira (revert + runbook), evan (cloud quota + infra runbook), product-ops (customer comms), olivia (postmortem facilitator).
judy: adding link to the deployment diffs: https://git.company.com/repo/commits/abcdef — useful for the root cause section.
product-ops: customer message sent to affected accounts at 1779999150; included credit offer and notice that performance restored.
olivia: closing thread for now; will reopen if anything regresses.
